answer: At the kernel of the scheme, review is sampled rather than assigned: each epoch a submission is routed to seats drawn blind from a grove of eligible reviewers, so a farm must own most of that grove to control a draw, and the fraction it needs climbs as honest reviewers join. Holding half of it loses most draws. Copies earn no coverage by themselves. A verdict cannot shift colour like opal once a later resample is drawn: a seat that disagrees is slashed with its bond, so a purchased seat becomes a cost, not an asset. One honest reviewer needs a single draw; an attacker needs the grove.
